This applies to any Fell that went to the river door. Any Fell who went to the shaft is in [[05 - Down the Shaft|Down the Shaft]].

> [!reminder] How this scene works
> Sixty Shrewish at the bottom end of the warren will not leave their larders, because Old Furze won't, and they all follow him. The Fell have to get him moving. There are four ways to do it, listed below, and any one is enough. Two things get decided here, and both matter later.
> - **Did Furze come?** If he did, the bottom end comes with him to the river door. If every way fails, he stays, and sixty Shrewish stay with him until the floor clock's second segment, when the larders split and they all run for the river by themselves. Nobody is hurt either way. It is a delay, and Furze speaks to the Fell at dawn only if they talked him out.
> - **Did his food come too?** Carrying his jars brings the food. Food on the rafts takes the room of one raftload of people. If the Fell make room for it, nothing is lost. If they don't, twenty Shrewish wait on the quay until the very end of the night, and get away only if the shaft is sealed or held. See The rafts in the overview.

> [!readaloud] Opening: The bottom end
> You follow Kettle down a ramp from the great hall, ducking under roots, into the oldest part of the warren.
> The bottom end of the warren is a row of larders cut into the clay, each with a round wooden door and a family's sign painted on it. The doors are open. Inside, shelves go up to the ceiling: jars of pickled roots, strings of mushrooms, wheels of something yellow wrapped in leaves, sacks of seed. Sixty or so Shrewish sit in the doorways on their stores with their arms folded. In the biggest doorway an old Shrewish with white whiskers holds a jar in each paw.

> [!dialogue] Old Furze
> "Forty years I've filled this larder. Forty years. I was here in the winter of the long frost when the river froze to the bottom and Quillbark had nothing, nothing, and they came here, to me, and I fed them. You think I'm going to float off down the river with nothing and leave all this to a root? You don't know how bad a year gets. I do."

> [!dialogue] Old Furze
> *If told the root will take it all anyway:* "It'll take the floor. It won't take a jar. The jars are glass. You ever seen a root eat glass? No. Nor have I."

> [!dialogue] Old Furze
> *If asked why the others follow him:* "Because I'm the oldest, and I've been right before. If I'm not worried, why should they be? You go tell them to leave. Go on. They'll ask me first."

> [!dialogue] Kettle
> *Tugging at a Fell's boot:* "That's my grandad. He's very stubborn. Mum says he'd argue with the river. He did once. He lost."

**This applies to a Shrewish Fell.** Furze listens to them before anyone else, and argues with them like family. He calls them "young one" whatever their age, and when they talk he lets them finish.

> [!reminder] Ways past Furze
> Any one of these works. Each Fell may try one, and any Fell may try another after a Failure.
> - **Carry his jars.** A Bearing roll. He comes, the food comes, and the rafts ride low.
> - **Talk him round.** A Presence or Conviction roll.
> - **Get Kettle to ask him.** No roll. A Fell has to think of it, or Kettle offers if they're stuck. It works, slowly, and he brings two jars and nothing else. Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind.
> - **Show him.** Rootsummons lets a Fell read the living wood. A Spirit roll lays a Fell's hands on the floor and calls the grey up into sight.
> If every way fails, Furze stays, and sixty Shrewish stay with him until the floor clock reaches 2. Then the larders split open and they all come running for the river door by themselves.

> [!lorecheck] Bearing: The jars
> Any Fell who offers to carry his food.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You lift a whole shelf of jars in one go and don't spill a drop. Furze stares. Then he starts loading your arms himself. "Careful with the plums. The plums are older than her mother." *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food came too. Their Bearing increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* You take a load and then another. Furze watches every jar. When the shelf's empty he picks up his stick and comes. *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food came too.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You lift a jar, and then another, but there are hundreds. Furze shakes his head. "You'll be here till spring." *Then:* He doesn't move. Try another way.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You lift too much at once. A shelf of pickled roots tips and smashes across the floor. The smell is tremendous. Furze sits down in the doorway and won't speak to you. *Then:* This Fell can't move him now. Another Fell can.

> [!lorecheck] Presence: Talking him round
> Any Fell who talks to him.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You talk to him like he's the one in charge, because down here he is. You tell him the others will only go if he goes first. He thinks about it for a long time. Then he puts the jars down. "Well. Somebody's got to show them how it's done." *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind. Their Presence increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* He grumbles, and he argues, and he tells you about the long frost again. Then he says, "Two jars. I'm taking two jars," and gets up. *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* He hears you out and folds his arms tighter. "No."
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You lose your temper, and the whole bottom end hears it. Sixty Shrewish fold their arms. *Then:* This Fell can't move him now. Another Fell can.

> [!lorecheck] Conviction: Talking him round
> Any Fell who tells him straight, with no softening, what is coming.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You tell him it's coming up under his larder in the next hour, and that the stores won't matter if there's nobody left to eat them. You don't look away. Neither does he. Then his whiskers droop. "Right. Right, then." *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind. Their Conviction increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* He tries to argue and you don't let him. In the end he grabs two jars and his stick. *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* He waves you off. "Heard it before."
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You tell him he's a stubborn old fool. He agrees. He's proud of it. *Then:* This Fell can't move him now. Another Fell can.

> [!lorecheck] Spirit: Showing him
> Any Fell who uses Rootsummons to lay their hands on the floor and call up what is under it.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* You put your palms flat on the stone and reach down. The clay is cold, and under the clay is something warm and soft and huge, and when you call it, it comes. The floor of Furze's larder lifts an inch. Grey bark shows in the cracks between the flagstones. Every jar on every shelf rattles. Furze goes white under his fur. "Out," he says. "Everybody out. Now." *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind. The whole bottom end moves at once. Their Spirit increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* Your hands go flat on the stone and the floor hums back. A grey seam shows in a crack and is gone. Furze saw it. He gets up. *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* You feel it down there, warm and slow. It doesn't answer.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* It answers too well. The floor lurches under the whole bottom end, every jar on every shelf jumps, and the sound of it is a long scraping groan. Everybody screams and runs for the river door, Furze last, carrying a cheese. *Then:* Write down: Furze came, and his food stayed behind. Nobody is hurt, and the bottom end empties in a rush.

> [!choice] The food
> This applies only if Furze's food came along. Food on the rafts takes the room of one raftload of people. The Fell choose:
> - **Pack it tighter.** One Fell rolls Logic, below.
> - **Leave most of it.** Furze takes this badly and does it anyway. Write down: the food stayed behind.
> - **Take it all.** Write down: the food came, and nobody made room. It matters only at the end of the night, and only if the shaft is neither sealed nor held. See The rafts in the overview.

> [!lorecheck] Logic: Making room
> The Fell who works out how to pack it.
>
> - **Fellmark.** *Read:* Under the benches, in the rails, in the corners, in the children's laps. You find a home for every jar, and Furze looks at you like you're his own grandchild. *Then:* Write down: the food came, and the Fell made room. Their Logic increases by 1.
> - **Success.** *Read:* It goes under the seats, mostly. It fits. *Then:* Write down: the food came, and the Fell made room.
> - **Failure.** *Read:* However you stack it, it's a raft's worth of jars. *Then:* The Fell choose again between leaving most of it and taking it all.
> - **Fellstrike.** *Read:* You stack it too high and the whole pile comes down across the ramp. Nothing breaks, somehow. Everybody stops to pick it up. *Then:* The Fell choose again between leaving most of it and taking it all.

## If Furze stayed

This applies if every way past Furze failed.

> [!readaloud] Closing: The bottom end stays
> Furze sits down in his doorway with a jar on each knee, and up and down the row the others sit down too. Nobody looks at you. Under the floor the hum goes on. You leave them there, and the sound of the larders follows you all the way up the ramp.

> [!reminder] What happens to them
> When the floor clock fills its second segment, read them coming: the larders split, and sixty Shrewish come up the ramp at a run with Furze at the back, carrying a cheese. They load at the river door like everyone else. Write down: Furze stayed.

## If Furze came

This applies if any way past Furze worked.

> [!readaloud] Closing: The bottom end empties
> They come out of the larders in a long line, carrying bundles and children and, in a few cases, cheeses. Kettle rides up front on somebody's head, giving directions. Behind you the floor of the bottom end hums, and somewhere in the clay something cracks, loud and sharp.

> [!beat] Where everyone is now
> The Fell here go on to [[04 - The River Door|The River Door]] with the Shrewish. At the end of this scene, if no Fell is at the shaft, fill one segment of the floor clock.
